quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Why should you not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses clearly in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles. If you stop suddenly in front of a large vehicle, the driver may not have time to stop and could hit you.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle breaks down?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on your hazard lights.
Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, move it off the road if you can. Turn on your emergency lights so other drivers can see that you are having trouble.

questions.question: On a slippery road, how far should you follow the car ahead?
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, your vehicle needs more distance to stop. Always keep a longer distance between your car and the car ahead.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal when turning from this lane.
Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. If you are turning in that direction, prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic pass before you turn.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign shows a steep hill is coming. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Areas in your vision that get worse when you are tired.
Areas on the road you cannot see in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas on the road you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in blind spots. These are areas near the rear corners of your vehicle that your mirrors cannot show you.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC).
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body and reduces its effects.

questions.question: After drinking beer, how can you reduce alcohol's effects?
questions.explanation: Only waiting will reduce alcohol's effects. Cold showers and coffee do not speed up this process. It takes about one hour for your body to remove the effects of one drink.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The bed of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: Children age 12 and under should always sit in the back seat. Airbags can hurt children if they are in the front seat.

questions.question: This is the shape and color of a ____ sign.
questions.explanation: Triangular signs pointing down mean yield. Slow down when you see a yield sign. Stop if you need to. If you stop, do so at the marked stop line.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must stop completely at the stop line. Only move when it is safe. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk or intersection.

questions.question: You should yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
Only if the traffic lights are in the pedestrian's favor.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: If a traffic signal light is green and a police officer signals for you to stop, you should:

options.text: Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's signals, even if they conflict with traffic lights or signs.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. You must stop completely. Do not proceed until it is safe to pass through the intersection.

questions.question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
questions.explanation: When the road is wet, snowy, or icy, your tires do not grip as well. Slow down to stay safe.

questions.question: If you are driving and you see animals standing near the roadway:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see animals near the road. They may suddenly move or change direction. There may also be more animals you cannot see.

questions.question: If you approach a stopped school bus that has its lights flashing and signal arm extended, you should:

options.text: Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.
Proceed at normal speed, but watch for children.

questions.explanation: You must stop completely when a school bus has flashing lights and an extended signal arm. Stay stopped until the arm is pulled back and the bus moves. This applies whether you are behind or across from the bus.

questions.question: To help others see you when daylight begins to fade, you should use your:
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beam headlights when daylight starts to fade. Only use high beams in open areas when no other drivers are nearby.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.

questions.explanation: Create a habit for getting in and out of your car. Before starting the car, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: When a railroad crossing gate is coming down, you should:

options.text: Speed up and cross the tracks before the gate closes.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing if the gate is coming down. Any other action is unsafe.

questions.question: When rain or fog makes it hard to see, drivers should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams bounce off the water or fog and reflect back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians who use guide dogs or white canes (with or without a red tip) have the right-of-way at all times. Always give them space to cross.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow down to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and a stop arm out, students are getting on or off. Do not move until the lights stop flashing and the arm is pulled in. Never pass a school bus that is loading or unloading students.

questions.question: There is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane ahead. You should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the pedestrian and then pass them.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane, even if there is no crosswalk. Give them space to finish crossing safely.

questions.question: As the percentage of alcohol in your blood increases, you become:
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the amount of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: When taking any medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor about side effects before you drive.
Keep your window open and drive slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor about side effects before you drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your ability to drive safely. Always talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how a medicine might affect your driving, especially sedatives and tranquilizers.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You should use cruise control near a railroad crossing to keep a steady speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Always be careful near railroad tracks.

questions.question: Mississippi law requires headlights to be used:

options.text: When the temperature drops below freezing.

questions.explanation: Mississippi law requires headlights to be on between sunset and sunrise. You must also use low beams when you are within 500 feet of another vehicle coming toward you or following you.
